comments.value: This can be fixed by making sure that you don't pull variables from branches that may or may not execute. In this case, the gameobject get transform node happens in the first branch, and then all the other branches pull from that. If it is separated so each branch has it's own gameobject get transform node, then it works just fine.
@{5b7fb61894211b58b866e8ae|full_name}: I fixed it doing this. I'm not sure if this is an udon issue or not

@{58d2df84430f4652e88c5666|full_name}: Based on the flow and what Phasedragon just explained it looks to be an Udon issue as one would expect the three flow lines from the original get transform node to be duplicated for each branch allowing each to work independently. 
I understand Udon trying to optimise the calls like that but in this case it should probably not have tried to take three separate flows and turned it into one.

@{5b7fb61894211b58b866e8ae|full_name}: I really hope its not an intended workflow to have the user physically duplicate the nodes when the flow lines indicate that the code/nodes should be duplicated already.

details:
ok so, I made this graph in 3 different ways. each version has the exact same bug.
I made a universal transform setter for gameobjects, like teleportto in triggers, but, this lets you chose if you want to copy the position, rotation and/or scale of the reference object.
in all 3 ways I tried to make this, if whatever the first option is is set to false, it fails the other two, such as, in my examples, if position is set to false, rotation and scale fail.
When I swapped it so rotation was first in the block, if rotation is false it fails, but, as long as rotation was on, it works no matter what other two are on or off

VRCSDK3-2020.01.14.10.40
